thread_text:
ellen: Heads up — SF office HVAC went out, facilities told us to close at 2pm. If I leave early, should I file PTO or can I take comp time?

ravi: If you were scheduled onsite and need to leave, take PTO unless you have previously banked comp. I can approve comp only if you worked extra hours last week and we agreed. ping me with hours.

sam (People Ops): Short policy note: for partial-day emergency closures we generally ask folks to use PTO or a floating holiday. Comp-time requires prior accrual and manager sign-off. Exceptions can be made in one-off cases — managers should include a brief note when approving.

sam (People Ops): How to log it: HR Portal -> Time Off -> Select "Partial Day" or "Floating Holiday" -> add note "Office closure - HVAC" and tag your manager. If comp is approved, choose time code "Comp-Off" and attach manager approval screenshot. Example note: "Office closed by facilities, approved comp by Ravi 3/22"

ellen: ok thanks — I don't have any banked comp so I'll submit PTO.

jena: For clarity — if team agreed to pay people to go home (admin pay), managers should send a quick email to payroll@redwood with list + hours. payroll-bot will pick it up.

payroll-bot: Got it — please use code COMPOFF for comp time entries. If admin pay requested, managers must CC payroll@redwood and include employee IDs + hours. Link to form: https://hr.redwood.example/office-closure-form

maria: quick question: if someone swapped shifts earlier in the week and worked extra, can we still mark comp?

sam (People Ops): Yes, provided there's a record of the extra hours (timesheet or manager confirmation). Manager should approve in the portal and add the reason.

ravi: Approved comp for Ellen for 2 hours. Ellen I put the note in the HR portal. :thumbsup:

ellen: thanks! filing PTO for the remainder. Appreciate the quick answers everyone. :heart:
